transcript.text: Start by inspecting the files. for f in ['chart.py','summary.txt','table.csv']: print('=== ',f); print(open(f).read()) continue

Found three faults in chart.py. First, the code filters out every Part_time row, so the red series the summary describes never appears. Second, the title says "Annual Leave Days" when the chart shows Weekly Work Hours. Third, the hardcoded raw data doesn't match table.csv: it has 15 full-time and 5 part-time countries, while the table has 6 full-time and 4 part-time. The fix is to build the histogram from table.csv instead. I'll melt the table into long form and sum the counts with histfunc='sum'. The bins will be 2 hours wide from 35 to 45, so each bin is centred on the 36/38/40/42/44 values. I'll correct the title and keep the colours, overlay mode, layout and legend unchanged. src = open('chart.py').read() new = '''import plotly.express as px import pandas as pd table = pd.read_csv('table.csv') df = table.melt(id_vars='Weekly_Work_Hours', value_vars=['Full_time_Count', 'Part_time_Count'], var_name='Employment_Type', value_name='Count') df['Employment_Type'] = df['Employment_Type'].str.replace('_Count', '', regex=False) df = df.rename(columns={'Weekly_Work_Hours': 'Work_Hours_Per_Week'}) fig = px.histogram( df, x='Work_Hours_Per_Week', y='Count', histfunc='sum', color='Employment_Type', title='Distribution of Weekly Work Hours by Employment Type (2013)', labels={'Work_Hours_Per_Week': 'Weekly Work Hours', 'count': 'Number of Countries'}, color_discrete_map={'Full_time': '#636EFA', 'Part_time': '#EF553B'}, opacity=0.8, barmode='overlay' ) fig.update_traces(xbins=dict(start=35, end=45, size=2)) fig.update_yaxes(title_text='Number of Countries') fig.update_layout( autosize=False, width=1000, height=600, margin=dict(l=50, r=50, b=50, t=50, pad=20), legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1) ) fig.write_image('output.png') ''' with open('chart.py','w') as f: f.write(new) exec(new) for t in fig.data: print(t.name, list(t.x), list(t.y)) print(fig.layout.title.text) continue
